title: Transient Affinity Router with Capacity Tokenization for Multi-Region Stability
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a transient affinity router that issues short-lived locality 'capacity tokens' to steer requests toward preferred regions while preserving global SLOs and enabling graceful shed/failover behavior. This ticket covers design, prototyping, infra changes, and rollout for the router plus the token accounting subsystem. The goal is to reduce p95 tail latency and avoid large-scale cross-region evictions when an edge or region experiences transient congestion.
acceptance_criteria: Router can issue and validate capacity tokens with <= 2ms overhead per request in the fast-path
Default affinity window (token TTL) is configurable and defaults to 30s
When local capacity drops below threshold, router reduces affinity by reclaiming tokens and triggers circuit-breaker policy before cross-region hedging
End-to-end p95 latency for regional traffic improves by at least 10% in our synthetic workload compared to current greedy geo-pin baseline
Telemetry exposes token issuance rate, token hit ratio, per-region token debt, and number of requests forced to remote regions
Can be rolled back by flipping config flag without requiring infra redeploy
design_notes: Concept: token = transient grant of 'local preferred capacity' assigned to a client's routing fingerprint. Tokens live in central token-store with region-local caches for fast validation.

Affinity semantics: clients with valid token routed to preferred region unless the region reports 'token deficit' > X%; in deficit state token validation returns soft-fail which allows broker to apply capacity-aware reweighting.

Token lifecycle: issued on success responses when upstream region latency and load are healthy. TTL short to limit stickiness during oscillations. Reissue logic uses moving-average of p95 and accept-rate.
Capacity accounting: regions publish 'capacity credits' per model/instance-class. Token issuance consumes credits; credits replenish via autoscaler signals and scheduled buckets.

Circuit breakers & shedding: combine token deficits with queue-depth and CPU pressure signals to escalate from local backpressure -> partial rejection -> cross-region hedging -> failover. Rejection policy prefers degraded model variants before remote routing.

Failover ordering: 1) honor local cache if healthy; 2) attempt token borrow from adjacent region if within safe RTT and capacity; 3) hedged fanout for critical requests with adaptive timeout; 4) full failover to backup region.
Safety: conservative defaults to avoid global thrashing; token issuance is rate-limited per customer and per-route to limit warm-up storms. Strong circuit-breaker hysteresis to avoid ping-ponging.
APIs: router exposes /token/issue, /token/validate, /token/revoke and telemetry endpoints. All APIs are authenticated and audited.
implementation_tasks: Prototype token-store using Redis Cluster with region-local read replica cache (ENG-branch: feat/transient-tokens)
Add token header propagation to request path (x-rw-affinity-token) and fast-path validation in edge proxy
Integrate region capacity publisher: small agent running on allocator that posts capacity credits to control-plane topic
Router policy engine: implement evaluation order (token validation -> capacity check -> hedging decision -> circuit breaker) in gait-controller component
Add unit and integration tests for token TTL, token theft/duplication scenarios, and token revocation flows
Instrument telemetry and dashboards (Grafana): token issuance, hit-rate, per-region debt, cross-region ratio, hedged-request count
Create migration toggle behind runtime feature flag and config with safe rollback
Prepare deployment playbook and runbook for on-call to respond to regressions
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics: affinity_token_issued_total, affinity_token_validation_latency_ms, affinity_token_hit_ratio, region_capacity_credits, region_token_debt_percent, hedged_requests_total, cross_region_failovers_total
SLOs to watch: p95 request latency per-region, cross-region traffic percentage (aim < 12% for non-fallback scenarios), token_validation_error_rate < 0.1%
Alerts: token_debt_percent > 20% for > 2m -> Pager (P1); hedged_requests_total spike > 3x baseline -> Pager (P1); token validation latency > 10ms median -> SRE Review (P2)
Dashboards: per-customer token churn, token TTL distribution, region credit consumption heatmap, circuit-breaker state timeline
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy token-store and router feature gated to 1% of traffic in us-west with internal-only tenants (1 day)
Phase 1 (expanded canary): expand to 10% across us-west and eu-west traffic using synthetic load and a select set of customers (3 days)
Phase 2 (gradual ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with checks at each step and automatic rollback on pager triggers
Fallbacks: flip runtime flag, revoke tokens globally, and fall back to legacy pin-and-hedge; documented rollback steps in runbook
Post-rollout: 1-week burn period monitoring token debt and customer SLOs then schedule retrospective
qa_plan: Load tests simulating 10% sudden capacity drop in primary region to validate graceful degradation and token reclamation
Chaos test: pause autoscaler in canary region and validate circuit-breaker prevents global thrash
A/B evaluation: compare p95 and cross-region ratios between tokenized routing and legacy routing for matched customer cohorts
Security review of token propagation to ensure no PII leakage and validate signing/encryption for tokens
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Token-store becomes availability bottleneck -> Mitigation: region-local replica and read-through cache + fallback to stateless soft-affinity when store is unreachable
Risk: Oscillation between regions due to aggressive TTLs -> Mitigation: conservative default TTL (30s) + increase hysteresis and require multi-window confirmation to revoke tokens
Risk: Malicious clients hoarding tokens -> Mitigation: per-customer token quota, token issuance rate limits, and audit logs with automated anomaly detection
Risk: Increased cross-region egress costs if hedging misfires -> Mitigation: cost-aware weighting applied to hedged requests and prefer degraded model variant locally before remote routing
